title: A path into the forest
goal: Organise repeated trees around a receding path.
kit: 2H, HB, 2B, 4B, 6B; kneaded eraser; clean stump; medium-tooth paper.

steps.title: Study the reference
steps.text: Find the light path, middle-distance trees and dark near trunks. Squint to ignore individual leaves.
steps.talk: Study the reference. Find the light path, middle-distance trees and dark near trunks. Squint to ignore individual leaves. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does the path lead toward a clear distance?
steps.check: Does the path lead toward a clear distance?

steps.title: Light block-in
steps.text: Place the path’s converging sides and its narrow distant end. Add the largest trunk positions.
steps.talk: Light block-in. Place the path’s converging sides and its narrow distant end. Add the largest trunk positions. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does the path narrow consistently?

steps.title: Refine the construction
steps.text: Vary trunk widths and intervals. Avoid symmetrical rows or identical crowns.
steps.talk: Refine the construction. Vary trunk widths and intervals. Avoid symmetrical rows or identical crowns. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the near trees larger?

steps.title: Three-value map
steps.text: Keep the path light, distant foliage midtone and foreground trunks dark.
steps.talk: Three-value map. Keep the path light, distant foliage midtone and foreground trunks dark. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Is the light path continuous?

steps.title: Five values and layers
steps.text: Layer the nearest trunks and undergrowth. Reduce contrast and detail in the distance.
steps.talk: Five values and layers. Layer the nearest trunks and undergrowth. Reduce contrast and detail in the distance. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Is the distance visibly quieter?

steps.title: Selective blending
steps.text: Soften distant foliage lightly; leave selected foreground trunk edges clear.
steps.talk: Selective blending. Soften distant foliage lightly; leave selected foreground trunk edges clear. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Do softer edges support depth?

steps.title: Lift the lights
steps.text: Lift broken light patches on the path. Vary their size and keep them smaller farther away.
steps.talk: Lift the lights. Lift broken light patches on the path. Vary their size and keep them smaller farther away. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Do the light patches sit on the ground?
steps.check: Do the light patches sit on the ground?

steps.title: Texture and detail
steps.text: Add a few bark marks and near leaves. Follow trunk direction and group foliage into masses.
steps.talk: Texture and detail. Add a few bark marks and near leaves. Follow trunk direction and group foliage into masses. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are most leaves implied rather than individually outlined?
steps.check: Are most leaves implied rather than individually outlined?

steps.title: Final accents and edges
steps.text: Deepen the nearest contact shadows and reduce distracting marks at the sides.
steps.talk: Final accents and edges. Deepen the nearest contact shadows and reduce distracting marks at the sides. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does your eye follow the path into the picture?
steps.check: Does your eye follow the path into the picture?

source: Original AI-generated graphite reference. Intermediate images are analytical contour and value views of this same reference, not hand-drawn stages.
drill: Repeat the study at half size without the grid. Compare your darkest dark, lightest light and largest shape before adding detail.
